```{ojs}
//| output: false
// Applies the selected example's params to the fields above and clicks
// Run, in place — no page reload, so no scroll jump either. A plain
// "change" listener attached once to the stable native <select> (rather
// than an OJS cell reactive on exampleSelect's value) — a <select> fires
// both "input" and "change" per selection, and a reactive cell would run
// once per event, with two overlapping calls racing each other.
applyExampleFromSelect = {
  const nativeSelect = (viewof exampleSelect).querySelector("select")
  if (!nativeSelect) return
  nativeSelect.addEventListener("change", () => {
    const example = (viewof exampleSelect).value
    if (!example) return
    VM.ui.applyExampleParams(exampleFieldSelectors, example.params, viewof plotTrigger)
  })
}
```

```{ojs}
syncExampleFromFields = {
  NInput; TInput; JInput; hInput; seedInput; maxSweepsInput
  VM.ui.syncExampleSelect(viewof exampleSelect, examples, exampleFieldSelectors)
}
```

```{ojs}
//| output: false
// Enter in any of the commit-gated fields clicks Run instead of submitting
// the field's own (invisible) form. Depends only on the stable views, so
// this wiring runs once and is never re-attached.
enterToPlot = {
  for (const view of [viewof NInput, viewof TInput, viewof JInput, viewof hInput, viewof seedInput]) {
    const input = view.querySelector("input")
    if (!input) continue
    input.addEventListener("keydown", (e) => {
      if (e.key !== "Enter") return
      e.preventDefault()
      viewof plotTrigger.querySelector("button").click()
    })
  }
}
```

```{ojs}
//| output: false
// committed snapshots N/T/J/h/seed only when Run is clicked, and writes
// them back into the URL so the address bar stays a shareable link. It
// reads the stable `viewof` DOM views (not the reactive values), so it
// does NOT rerun on every keystroke — only when `plotTrigger` changes. It
// still runs once on initial page load, so the first render uses the
// URL-provided (or default) values with no click.
committed = {
  plotTrigger
  const math = window.math
  const NText = (viewof NInput).value
  const TText = (viewof TInput).value
  const JText = (viewof JInput).value
  const hText = (viewof hInput).value
  const seedText = (viewof seedInput).value

  const params = new URLSearchParams(window.location.search)
  params.set("N", NText)
  params.set("T", TText)
  params.set("J", JText)
  params.set("h", hText)
  params.set("seed", seedText)
  history.replaceState(null, "", `${window.location.pathname}?${params}`)

  // N is rounded and clamped here (not just parsed): unlike a scalar field
  // such as x0 in Newton's method, N drives an N×N simulation, so an
  // unclamped value could hang the tab. [2, 100] keeps the worst case (100
  // × 100 lattice, 2000 sweeps — see maxSweeps below) well under a second.
  let NVal = VM.expressions.makeNumber(math, NText)
  if (Number.isFinite(NVal)) NVal = Math.max(2, Math.min(100, Math.round(NVal)))

  return {
    N: NVal,
    T: VM.expressions.makeNumber(math, TText),
    J: VM.expressions.makeNumber(math, JText),
    h: VM.expressions.makeNumber(math, hText),
    seed: VM.expressions.makeNumber(math, seedText)
  }
}
```

```{ojs}
urlSyncControls = {

  params.set("max", maxSweepsInput)
  history.replaceState(null, "", `${window.location.pathname}?${params}`)
  return true
```

```{ojs}
//| output: false
// maxSweeps parses the Max sweeps field's expression, falling back to 200
// for invalid input. Clamped to 2000: each sweep is N² attempted flips
// plus an O(N²) energy/magnetization recompute, and a snapshot of the
// whole lattice is stored every sweep — an unclamped value here, combined
// with a large N, could take the tab down.
maxSweeps = {
  const parsed = VM.expressions.makeNumber(window.math, maxSweepsInput)
  if (parsed === null || !Number.isFinite(parsed)) return 200
  return Math.max(1, Math.min(2000, Math.round(parsed)))
}
```

```{ojs}
//| output: false
// result: runs single-spin-flip Metropolis dynamics on an N×N lattice with
// periodic boundary conditions (a torus — each site's four neighbors wrap
// around both edges) for maxSweeps sweeps, one sweep being N² randomly
// chosen single-spin flip attempts. Starts from a random ("hot") initial
// configuration, seeded so the whole run is reproducible from the URL.
//   rows — one entry per sweep (0 = the initial state): { sweep, grid,
//     energy, magnetization, acceptRate }. grid is a flat Int8Array of ±1,
//     row-major (index = y*N + x); energy and magnetization are already
//     divided by N² (per site); acceptRate is null for sweep 0.
//   N — the lattice size actually used (0 if parsed is false)
//   parsed — false when N, T, J, h, or seed couldn't be read
result = {
  const N = committed.N
  const T = committed.T
  const J = committed.J
  const h = committed.h
  const seed = committed.seed

  const valid = Number.isFinite(N) && N >= 2 && Number.isFinite(T) && T >= 0 && Number.isFinite(J) && Number.isFinite(h) && Number.isFinite(seed)
  if (!valid) return {rows: [], N: 0, parsed: false}

  const rng = VM.sampling.seededRandom(Math.round(seed))
  const size = N * N

  const grid = new Int8Array(size)
  for (let i = 0; i < size; i++) grid[i] = rng() < 0.5 ? -1 : 1

  // Sum of the four periodic neighbors of (x, y) — wrap-around is what
  // makes this a torus rather than a plain square with an edge.
  const neighborSum = (x, y) => {
    const xm = (x - 1 + N) % N, xp = (x + 1) % N
    const ym = (y - 1 + N) % N, yp = (y + 1) % N
    return grid[y * N + xm] + grid[y * N + xp] + grid[ym * N + x] + grid[yp * N + x]
  }

  // Each bond counted once: the bond to the right and the bond below every
  // site covers every edge of the periodic lattice exactly once.
  const totalEnergy = () => {
    let e = 0
    for (let y = 0; y < N; y++) {
      for (let x = 0; x < N; x++) {
        const s = grid[y * N + x]
        const right = grid[y * N + (x + 1) % N]
        const down = grid[((y + 1) % N) * N + x]
        e += -J * s * (right + down) - h * s
      }
    }
    return e
  }

  const totalMagnetization = () => {
    let m = 0
    for (let i = 0; i < size; i++) m += grid[i]
    return m
  }

  const rows = []
  rows.push({sweep: 0, grid: grid.slice(), energy: totalEnergy() / size, magnetization: totalMagnetization() / size, acceptRate: null})

  for (let sweep = 1; sweep <= maxSweeps; sweep++) {
    let accepted = 0
    for (let k = 0; k < size; k++) {
      // A randomly chosen site each attempt (not a fixed scan order) is
      // the standard single-spin-flip Metropolis sweep.
      const x = Math.floor(rng() * N)
      const y = Math.floor(rng() * N)
      const i = y * N + x
      const s = grid[i]

      // Flipping s -> -s changes the energy by ΔE = 2 s (J Σ_neighbors + h).
      const localField = J * neighborSum(x, y) + h
      const deltaE = 2 * s * localField

      let accept = deltaE <= 0
      if (!accept && T > 0) accept = rng() < Math.exp(-deltaE / T)
      // T === 0: zero-temperature (greedy) dynamics — only accept if it
      // lowers the energy, never by chance.

      if (accept) {
        grid[i] = -s
        accepted++
      }
    }
    rows.push({sweep, grid: grid.slice(), energy: totalEnergy() / size, magnetization: totalMagnetization() / size, acceptRate: accepted / size})
  }

  return {rows, N, parsed: true}
}
```

```{ojs}
//| output: false
// setup picks the lattice snapshot visible at the current sweep.
setup = {
  const rows = result.rows
  if (rows.length === 0) return {row: null, N: 0, parsed: result.parsed}
  const idx = Math.max(0, Math.min(Math.round(stepControl), rows.length - 1))
  return {row: rows[idx], N: result.N, parsed: result.parsed}
}
```

```{ojs}
//| output: false
// mainPlot draws the current sweep's lattice as a two-color heatmap: one
// color per spin value. _plotDiv is kept in a closure so Plotly reuses the
// same DOM node across reactive re-renders (Plotly.react instead of
// Plotly.newPlot after the first render) — this preserves zoom/pan when
// the sweep slider moves.
mainPlot = {
  const Plotly = window.Plotly
  let _plotDiv = null

  return ({row, N, parsed}) => {
    const data = []

    if (row) {
      const z = []
      for (let y = 0; y < N; y++) {
        const line = []
        for (let x = 0; x < N; x++) line.push(row.grid[y * N + x])
        z.push(line)
      }
      data.push({
        z, type: "heatmap", zmin: -1, zmax: 1,
        // A two-stop discrete colorscale (each color repeated at the 0.5
        // boundary) rather than a continuous one — spin is binary, not a
        // smoothly varying quantity.
        colorscale: [[0, chartColors.alt], [0.5, chartColors.alt], [0.5, chartColors.fn], [1, chartColors.fn]],
        showscale: false,
        hovertemplate: "(x, y) = (%{x}, %{y})<br>spin = %{z:+d}<extra></extra>"
      })
    }

    const layout = {
      xaxis: {title: "x (mod N)", range: [-0.5, N - 0.5], showgrid: false, zeroline: false, scaleanchor: "y", constrain: "domain"},
      yaxis: {title: "y (mod N)", range: [-0.5, N - 0.5], showgrid: false, zeroline: false},
      annotations: parsed ? [] : VM.plotting.emptyState("Couldn't read that — check N, T, J, h, and the seed."),
      hovermode: "closest",
      uirevision: "static",
      autosize: true
    }
    const config = VM.plotting.config()

    if (!_plotDiv) {
      _plotDiv = document.createElement("div")
      _plotDiv.className = "plotly-box-large"
      Plotly.newPlot(_plotDiv, data, layout, config)
      // newPlot fires before the div is in the DOM, so Plotly measures 0 width.
      // A ResizeObserver catches the real size once it's inserted and laid out,
      // and keeps correcting it on any later layout/viewport change.
      VM.plotting.autoResize(_plotDiv)
    } else {
      Plotly.react(_plotDiv, data, layout, config)
    }
    return _plotDiv
  }
}
```

```{ojs}
// iteratesPlot draws the energy per site against the sweep number, for the
// entire run — it doesn't depend on the current step. Starting from a
// random configuration, this falls (for T below Tc) from near 0 toward the
// ordered ground-state energy as the lattice relaxes.
iteratesPlot = {
  const points = []
  for (const r of result.rows) points.push({sweep: r.sweep, energy: r.energy})
  return Plot.plot(VM.plotting.plotOptions({
    height: 260,
    x: {label: "sweep"},
    y: {label: "energy / site"},
    marks: [
      Plot.line(points, {x: "sweep", y: "energy", stroke: chartColors.fn}),
      Plot.dot(points, {x: "sweep", y: "energy", fill: chartColors.fn, r: 2.5})
    ]
  }))
}
```

```{ojs}
// convergencePlot draws |magnetization| per site against the sweep number,
// raw and as a running mean (VM.mcmc.runningMean) — the quantity a Monte
// Carlo estimate of the equilibrium magnetization converges through. Below
// Tc the raw series settles near one of the two ordered values (the finite
// lattice spontaneously picks a sign); above Tc it fluctuates around 0.
convergencePlot = {
  const rawPoints = []
  const absMagnetization = []
  for (const r of result.rows) {
    rawPoints.push({sweep: r.sweep, m: r.magnetization})
    absMagnetization.push(Math.abs(r.magnetization))
  }
  const running = VM.mcmc.runningMean(absMagnetization)
  const runningPoints = []
  for (let i = 0; i < running.length; i++) runningPoints.push({sweep: result.rows[i].sweep, m: running[i]})

  const rawName = "magnetization / site"
  const runName = "running mean of |magnetization| / site"
  const colorDomain = [rawName, runName]
  const colorRange = [chartColors.alt, chartColors.accent2]

  const chart = Plot.plot(VM.plotting.plotOptions({
    height: 260,
    x: {label: "sweep"},
    y: {label: "magnetization / site"},
    color: {domain: colorDomain, range: colorRange},
    marks: [
      Plot.dot(rawPoints, {x: "sweep", y: "m", fill: () => rawName, r: 2.5, opacity: 0.5}),
      Plot.line(runningPoints, {x: "sweep", y: "m", stroke: () => runName, strokeWidth: 2.5})
    ]
  }))

  const container = document.createElement("div")
  container.append(chart)
  container.append(Plot.legend({color: {domain: colorDomain, range: colorRange}}))
  return container
}
```

```{ojs}
// Sweep table — shows the entire run, not just the current step.
iterationTable = {
  if (result.rows.length === 0) {
    // Always return a Node so Quarto's OJS runtime never latches this
    // declaration cell as hidden.
    return document.createElement("div")
  }

  const formattedRows = []
  for (const row of result.rows) {
    const energyCell = row.energy.toPrecision(6)
    const magnetizationCell = row.magnetization.toPrecision(6)
    let acceptCell = "—"
    if (row.acceptRate !== null) acceptCell = (row.acceptRate * 100).toFixed(1) + "%"
    formattedRows.push([row.sweep, energyCell, magnetizationCell, acceptCell])
  }

  return VM.ui.renderTable({
    html,
    headers: ["Sweep", tex`E / N^2`, tex`M / N^2`, "Accepted flips"],
    csvHeaders: ["sweep", "energy_per_site", "magnetization_per_site", "accepted_flip_fraction"],
    filename: "ising-model-sweeps.csv",
    rows: formattedRows
  })
}
```

::::

The 2D Ising model places a spin $\sigma_i \in \{-1, +1\}$ on every site of a lattice. On an $N \times N$ **torus** — opposite edges identified, so site $(x, y)$'s neighbors wrap around both directions — every site has exactly four neighbors and there is no boundary to introduce edge effects. The energy of a configuration is

$$
H(\sigma) = -J \sum_{\langle i, j \rangle} \sigma_i \sigma_j - h \sum_i \sigma_i,
$$

summed over nearest-neighbor pairs $\langle i, j \rangle$. $J > 0$ favors aligned neighbors (<span class="vm-swatch vm-swatch-fn">ferromagnetic</span>), $J < 0$ favors anti-aligned ones (antiferromagnetic), and $h$ is a uniform external field.

The simulation above runs the **Metropolis algorithm**: each sweep attempts $N^2$ single-spin flips, each at a site chosen uniformly at random. Flipping the spin at that site changes the energy by $\Delta E = 2 \sigma_i \left( J \sum_{\text{neighbors}} \sigma_j + h \right)$, and the flip is accepted with probability $\min\!\left(1, e^{-\Delta E / T}\right)$ — always accepted if it lowers the energy, accepted with decreasing probability the more it raises it. This converges to the Boltzmann equilibrium distribution $P(\sigma) \propto e^{-H(\sigma)/T}$ at temperature $T$ (units with $k_B = 1$).

For $J = 1$, $h = 0$, and an infinite lattice, this model has an exact phase transition at the critical temperature

$$
T_c = \frac{2}{\ln(1 + \sqrt{2})} \approx 2.269,
$$

found by Onsager (1944). Below $T_c$ the lattice settles into one of two <span class="vm-swatch vm-swatch-fn">ordered</span> ground states (mostly spin-up or mostly spin-down — try the "Ordered phase" example); above $T_c$ thermal noise wins and spins point in <span class="vm-swatch vm-swatch-alt">random</span> directions with no net magnetization (the "Disordered phase" example). Near $T_c$ itself, clusters of aligned spins appear at every scale — the finite lattice's echo of the transition (the default view above, and the "Near the critical temperature" example).
